newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian stock gains on investment reforms.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian stock gains on investment reforms.

text.p: Shares on Jordan's stock exchange picked up again on Tuesday after Monday's profit-taking, rising nearly one percent in sustained optimism after the government passed two key investment reform laws this week.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 1.49 points to 153.33 points, its highest level for six weeks, after trade worth 1.06 million dinars ($1.5 million).
"The volume of trade was good and it was distributed among the blue-chips," said analyst Mohammad Abdallah of Pearl Consulting.
Arab Potash amd Jordan Phosphates both gained in heavy trade, rising 0.20 dinars and 0.13 dinars respectively.
Bank of Jordan, which has reopened plans for a merger with Jordan-Kuwait Bank, rose by 0.05 dinars to 3.10 dinars.

The AFM index had slipped back on Monday despite a boost to investors from the government's decision to approve laws cancelling a 15 percent tax on capital increases and allows the listing of mutual funds on the Amman bourse for the first time.
"Today there was more institutional demand," Abdallah said. "And it broadened out to all the blue-chip stocks."
Overall rising stocks outnumbered fallers by 17 to 12, with another 10 trading but closing unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.24 percent to 79.53 points, still 4.50 percent down from the start of the year.
